statement: Every child has a right to learn and can ask for help when school feels difficult.
explain: True. Learning matters, and a teacher, parent, caregiver, or another trusted adult can help you find support.

statement: Only children with perfect marks deserve to stay in school.
explain: False. Every child deserves a chance to learn. If school feels difficult, tell a trusted adult so they can help.

statement: If a secret makes you feel scared or uncomfortable, you can tell a trusted adult.
explain: True. You do not have to keep a secret that worries you. A trusted adult can listen and help.

statement: You should keep quiet if someone asks you to keep a secret about your body.
explain: False. You can tell a trusted adult. It is never your fault when someone asks you to keep an unsafe secret.

statement: Children need time for school, rest, play, and growing up safely.
explain: True. Children deserve time to learn, rest, and play. Tell a trusted adult if a child seems unsafe or cannot go to school.

statement: If harmful work keeps a child from school, it is the child’s fault.
explain: False. It is never a child’s fault. A trusted adult can help find safe support for the child.

statement: Keeping your password private is one way to stay safer online.
explain: True. Do not share passwords with strangers. If an online message worries you, show it to a trusted adult.

statement: You have to reply to an online message that makes you feel uneasy.
explain: False. You can stop replying and tell a trusted adult. In an immediate emergency, call 112 or ask an adult nearby to call.
